transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-09-14
Time: 11:00 - 11:42 AM ET
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Aisha Thompson (Rivermark Head of Platform), Ben Rivera (Rivermark SRE), Lina Gomez (Rivermark ML Eng)

Auto-summary: Quick sync on POC latency tuning. SE presented recent bench results; discussed TTFT regressions with seq_len=1024 and streaming behavior with small tokens. Action items assigned for deeper microbenchmarks and kernel experiments.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, uh let's do the usual quick rundown, maya you wanna kick off with the bench highlights?
[00:30] Maya: yeah sure, so we re-ran the TTFT tests on the 8xA800 pool, ran both the streaming pipeline and the single-shot generate path. overall median TTFT dropped from around 320ms to 230ms when we enabled continuous batching plus the new fused-kernel patch, but some of the 1024 seq runs still spike up near 480 to 520ms, so there's variability
[01:05] Ben: can i ask, the 8x A800, is that dedicated or your hosted instance? because we need to map to our dedicated cluster numbers
[01:13] Maya: this was on a dedicated-like config in our test harness, so it should be close to your reserved pool. slight diffs due to infra overlay but roughly comparable
[01:27] Aisha: our main concern is p50 under 200ms for the short-form queries, long tails are ok if they stay under 800ms, but p99 spikes will be a problem for some flows
[01:42] Jordan: noted. lina do you have the production seq length distro we talked about?
[01:48] Lina: yeah, we pushed the sample. about 68% under 128 tokens, 20% in 128-512, and around 12% above 512, very few above 2048. most conversational queries are 64-128
[02:05] Maya: ok that distribution helps a lot; it suggests optimizing for the 128 bucket and making sure streaming paths for small seqs are prioritized. TTFT improvements will come from warming the KV cache and enabling early prefix caching
[02:25] Ben: we also noticed that streaming sometimes increases end-to-end latency because of codec flushes on our side, so we need to test with your streaming chunk sizes
[02:33] Maya: right yes there's a chunking config. in our tests switching from 64-byte to 256-byte chunks reduced CPU overhead on client side and lowered end-to-end latency in most cases
[02:44] Jordan: quick question on kernels: maya you mentioned fused attention and flash-attn variants. what's the path forward there?
[02:52] Maya: so we tested two kernel sets — the standard cu-attn and then a fused attention build with flash-attn style kernels. fused build gave ~12-18% lower per-token latency on seqs >512, but for small seqs the overhead of fusion sometimes loses the benefit. also memory layout changes affect kv cache hits
[03:20] Lina: is there a compatibility risk with our quantized model format? we're using int8 with per-channel scales
[03:28] Maya: good call — fused kernels sometimes assume certain X/Y memory layouts; our team has a compatibility shim but we need to validate for your quantization profile. that's on my list to run this week
[03:38] Ben: and can we get visibility into GPU utilization percent in those runs? we saw bursty loads last week
[03:44] Maya: yes will include utilization traces; the run artifacts include p50/p90/p99 latencies, GPU util, and kernel launch logs. i'll attach the logs in the follow up
[04:00] Omar: side note — legal asked about data residency and logs retention, do you want us to share the SOC2+ISO packet now or later?
[04:07] Jordan: send it now please, we'll follow-up with our compliance pack and the SSO flow doc
[04:12] Aisha: great, thanks. back to benchmarks, what about batching? does increasing batch size help or hurt TTFT for our use case?
[04:20] Maya: good question — for TTFT we prefer small batch sizes or even single-request paths; batching helps throughput but increases per-request latency. we tested an adaptive strategy where the router disables batching for low-concurrency short requests and allows batching for background bulk rerank jobs
[04:40] Jordan: so the plan is to optimize routing policy to the 128 bucket and tune the batching threshold
[04:46] Maya: yep. also we want to try a streaming-first path where the model can emit tokens as soon as possible — that reduces perceived latency for users doing interactive flows
[04:56] Ben: how much improvement do you see with streaming-first?
[05:00] Maya: in our runs streaming-first cut user-perceived TTF by ~30% on small seqs, because we start emitting sooner, but server-side TTFT (time to first token from server) depends on initial kernel setup; that's where kernel warmup and persistent worker pools help
[05:18] Lina: is there a recommended warmup pattern? we've been doing cold starts per container
[05:23] Maya: persistent warm workers with periodic no-op requests, plus a small KV cache pre-populate using common prefixes. we can script the warmup for your traffic shape
[05:31] Jordan: ok next — latency regression we saw last week after enabling a new quantization pipeline. any ideas?
[05:38] Maya: suspect it's due to per-channel dequant op ordering; the quant pipeline introduced an extra memcpy in the hot path for some kernels. team is exploring moving the dequant earlier in the graph and eliminating the memcpy
[05:52] Ben: can that be solved in our stack or does it need a runtime change on your side?
[05:56] Maya: a bit of both; we can patch the runtime to skip the memcpy when formats match, but your model exporter could also produce a layout-friendly artifact
[06:08] Jordan: action item — maya to validate layout and run a tuned exporter, lina to share the model export config
[06:16] Maya: noted

[06:30] -- mid-call demo of microbench results shared (link: https://redwood-demo/runs/rvk-0914) --

[06:45] Maya: moving on to kernel selection, we recommended trying the fused-attn on the dedicated pool for the >512 tail. we can A/B and fall back to standard kernels if we see regressions
[07:10] Aisha: what's the rollback story? if fused-attn causes instability can we flip back quickly?
[07:16] Maya: yes, our rollout supports canarying by route and model version. we can set an automatic fallback policy at p95 threshold
[07:26] Ben: important to capture trace IDs for any failure, our SRE wants the end-to-end trace mapping
[07:32] Maya: we'll include trace hooks and map request ids back to your logs

[07:45] Jordan: ok let's talk scheduling — when can you run the TTFT microbenchmarks with the seq_len=1024 and streaming toggled on?
[07:52] Maya: i can kick those off today, target results by next tuesday
[07:56] Jordan: perfect

[08:10] -- brief sidebar about procurement timeline, AE picks up --

[08:22] Jordan: on pricing i'll push an updated pilot SOW that includes three weeks of dedicated benching and a small committed dev pool. should go out tomorrow
[08:32] Aisha: procurement prefers monthly billing cadence, we'll confirm with finance
[08:36] Jordan: understood

[08:44] -- customer asks a technical nit about TLS and KMS when running in Private --

[08:50] Maya: for Private we'll integrate with your KMS/HSM via our KMIP compatible connector; TLS termination is customer-managed in VPC, logs are forwarded to your SIEM, and audit logs are preserved
[09:06] Lina: any perf hit for KMS calls on inference path?
[09:11] Maya: typically we do crypto ops at session startup, not on per-request path; there is minimal impact. we'll share the compliance doc showing key rotation and latency expectations

[09:25] -- end of technical discussion --

[09:30] Jordan: recap — maya runs TTFT + streaming microbenchmarks (seq 512/1024), include GPU util and kernel traces; jordan to send pricing and SOW; aisha to share prod seq distro and model export config. we'll schedule kernel deep-dive next week. any other items?

[09:48] Aisha: sounds good
[09:52] Ben: good for us
[09:56] Jordan: thanks everyone, we can close, will follow up by email with links and logs

End of transcript
